He was drafted in the first round with the 11th overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], after playing [[college basketball]] for the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse Orange]]. He was named [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award|NBA Rookie of the Year]] in [[2013–14 NBA season|2014]], and he has also played for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], [[Chicago Bulls]], [[Charlotte Hornets]], [[Houston Rockets]], and [[Orlando Magic]]. ==High school career== Carter-Williams attended [[Hamilton-Wenham Regional High School]] in [[Hamilton, Massachusetts]] as a freshman. He was 5'9" as a freshman, and led his team and conference in scoring with 20 points per game and a league championship. In 2008, Carter-Williams transferred to the boarding school [[St. Andrew's School (Rhode Island)|St. Andrew's]] in [[Barrington, Rhode Island]] where he lived in a dormitory during his final three years of high school.{{cite web|url=http://dailyorange.com/2010/12/family-guy-basketball-roots-run-deep-for-syracuse-signee-carter-williams/|title=Family guy: Basketball roots run deep for Syracuse signee Carter-Williams|last=Irvin|first=Zuri|work=The Daily Orange|date=December 14, 2010|access-date=August 8, 2014}} In his three years as a starter, he averaged 25.4 points per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.suathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=9464|title=Michael Carter-Williams – 2012–13 Men's Basketball|work=suathletics.com|access-date=December 13, 2014}} As a senior, he averaged 23.2 points, 8.3 rebounds and 5.5 assists per game. After his sophomore season in high school, Carter-Williams committed to attend Syracuse where he played on their basketball team.{{cite web|url=http://www.newenglandrecruitingreport.com/news/article/1092/CarterWilliams-Big-East-Bound.php|title=Carter-Williams Big East Bound|publisher=New England Recruiting Report|date=November 2, 2009|access-date=September 28, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150220005535/http://www.newenglandrecruitingreport.com/news/article/1092/CarterWilliams-Big-East-Bound.php|archive-date=February 20, 2015|url-status=dead}} He visited colleges in August after his sophomore year in 2009 and received scholarship offers from other schools such as Providence, Virginia Tech, Florida State, Virginia, Notre Dame, and Clemson. Later in his high school career, he played on the same [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] team as future 76ers' teammate, [[Nerlens Noel]].{{cite web|url=http://sujuiceonline.com/2012/02/05/nerlens-noel-michael-carter-williams-syracuse-basketball/|title=Syracuse guard Carter-Williams talks about recruit Nerlens Noel|last=Cheng|first=Wes|work=The Juice|publisher=[[SportsNet New York]]|date=February 5, 2012|access-date=September 28, 2014}} [[File:Michael Carter-Williams.jpg|thumb|upright=0.9|Carter-Williams in 2010]] {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2011}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Michael Carter-Williams | position = [[Shooting guard|SG]] | hometown = Hamilton, Massachusetts | highschool = [[St. Andrew's School (Rhode Island)|St. Andrew's]] | feet = 6 | inches = 5 | weight = 175 | commitdate = 11/01/2009 | scout stars = 4 | rivals stars = 4 | espn grade = 97 }} {{College athlete recruit end | year = 2011 | rivals ref title = Syracuse 2011 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = 2011 Syracuse Basketball Commits | espn ref title = Syracuse Orange 2011 Player Commits | rivals school = syracuse | scout s = 185 | espn schoolid = 183 | scout overall = 9 (SG) | rivals overall = 29, 7 (SG) | espn overall = 21, 4 (SG), 6 (East) | accessdate = November 25, 2013 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Carter-Williams had a subdued freshman season at [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] in 2011–12 as he played behind [[Scoop Jardine]], [[Brandon Triche]] and [[Dion Waiters]]. The season began about how Carter-Williams envisioned with him coming off the bench but solidly in [[Jim Boeheim]]'s rotation. That niche role gradually eroded, however, as Jardine and Triche solidified their starting roles and Waiters emerged as the best sixth man in the nation. It was a difficult first season for him in which he did not play in games and received sporadic minutes in others.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/the-dagger/humbling-freshman-season-paved-way-michael-carter-williams-163418773--ncaab.html|title=A humbling freshman season paved the way for Michael Carter-Williams' sophomore success|work=[[Yahoo! Sports]]|publisher=Yahoo Inc.|last=Eisenberg|first=Jeff|date=December 13, 2012|access-date=November 1, 2014}} He finished the season averaging 2.7 points, 2.1 rebounds and 10.3 minutes in 26 total games (no starts).[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/michael-carter-williams-1.html Michael Carter-Williams Stats] [[File:MichaelCarterWillaims.jpg|thumb|upright=0.9|Carter-Williams warming up with Syracuse ahead of their game on the USS ''Midway'']] During the 2012 offseason, Carter-Williams worked on his game, from lifting weights daily and drinking protein shakes to try to get stronger, to doing shooting drills every morning and improving his nutrition. His hard work over the offseason translated into Carter-Williams' emergence as a breakout star for Syracuse and one of the best point guards in the nation during the 2012–13 season. He went on to start his first game for Syracuse in the season opener and kept his starting role for the entire season, starting all 40 games. He finished his sophomore season with averages of 11.9 points, 5.0 rebounds, 7.3 assists and 2.7 steals in 35.2 minutes per game. On March 28, 2013, he scored a career-high 24 points as he led Syracuse past the No. 1 seed Indiana Hoosiers 61–50 in the NCAA's East Region semi-finals as they advanced to the NCAA's Elite Eight.{{cite web|last=Waters|first=Mike|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2013/03/syracuse_downs_indiana_to_adva.html|title=Syracuse downs Indiana to advance to NCAA's Elite Eight|work=Syracuse.com|publisher=Syracuse Media Group|date=March 29, 2013|access-date=October 31, 2014}} At the conclusion of the season, he earned [[Associated Press]] honorable mention [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors, as well as second-team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]] honors. On April 10, 2013, Carter-Williams declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final two years of college eligibility.{{cite web|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2013/04/michael_carter-williams_declar.html|title=Syracuse basketball guard Michael Carter-Williams declares for the NBA Draft|work=Syracuse.com|publisher=Syracuse Media Group|last=Ditota|first=Donna|date=April 10, 2013|access-date=November 30, 2014}} ==Professional career== ===Philadelphia 76ers (2013–2015)=== ====2013–14 season: Rookie of the Year==== Many draft outlooks ranked Carter-Williams as a top point guard prospect and a top ten prospect overall.[http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Michael-Carter-Williams-6262/ Draft Express NBA Draft Prospect Profile][http://nbadraft.net/players/michael-carter-williams 1 – Michael Carter-Williams]{{cite web|url=https://insider.espn.com/nbadraft/results/top100/_/year/2013|title=Chad Ford's Top 100 – 2013|last=Ford|first=Chad|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=August 11, 2014}} Carter-Williams was selected 11th overall in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite press release|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-select-michael-carter-williams-11th-overall-pick-2013-nba-draft|title=Sixers Select Michael Carter-Williams with 11th Overall Pick in 2013 NBA Draft|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=June 28, 2013|access-date=August 11, 2014}} Carter-Williams, along with [[Nerlens Noel]], were both officially signed by the 76ers on September 24, 2013.{{cite press release|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/130924-noel-carter-williams-signed|title=Sixers Sign Nerlens Noel and Michael Carter-Williams|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=September 24, 2013|access-date=August 11, 2014}} On October 30, 2013, in his NBA debut, he recorded 22 points, 12 assists, 7 rebounds, and 9 steals (the most steals ever made by a rookie on debut) in a 114–110 win over the defending champion [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400488878|title=Michael Carter-Williams, 76ers hold on, stun Dwyane Wade-less Heat|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=ESPN|date=October 30, 2013|access-date=August 11, 2014}} Less than a week later, he had a 26-point, 10 assist performance in a 107–104 win over the Chicago Bulls. He was subsequently named the Player of the Week in only his first week in the NBA, a feat last achieved by [[Shaquille O'Neal]] in 1992.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/11/04/players-of-week-110413/|title=Carter-Williams, Love named Players of the Week|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=November 4, 2013|access-date=August 11, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131208052025/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/11/04/players-of-week-110413/|archive-date=December 8, 2013|url-status=dead}} On November 9, 2013, Carter-Williams recorded a career-high 13 assists to go with 21 points in a 127–125 double overtime loss to Cleveland.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20131109/PHICLE/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Cavaliers 127, Sixers 125 (2OT)|last=Dulik|first=Brian|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=November 9, 2013|access-date=August 11, 2014}} On December 3, 2013, he recorded his first triple-double with 27 points, 12 rebounds, and 10 assists in 47 minutes in a 126–125 double-overtime victory over the [[Orlando Magic]]. Rookie [[Victor Oladipo]] of the Magic also recorded his first career triple-double in the same game, marking the first and only time in NBA history that two rookies have recorded triple-doubles in the same game.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20131203/ORLPHI/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Sixers 126, Magic 125|last=Jasner|first=Andy|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=December 3, 2013|access-date=August 11, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131207092224/http://www.nba.com/games/20131203/ORLPHI/gameinfo.html|archive-date=December 7, 2013|url-status=dead}} The last time that two players had recorded their first career triple-doubles in the same game was when Detroit Pistons [[Donnie Butcher]] and [[Ray Scott (basketball)|Ray Scott]] did it on March 14, 1964 (they were not rookies). It was also the first time that two opponents had recorded triple-doubles in the same game since [[Caron Butler]] and [[Baron Davis]] had done so on November 23, 2007.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400489134|title=Michael Carter-Williams, 76ers overcome Arron Afflalo's 43|date=December 3, 2013|agency=Associated Press|publisher=ESPN|access-date=December 4, 2013}} Carter-Williams was named the Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month for games played in October and November 2013. He led all rookies in scoring (17.2 ppg), assists (7.3 apg), steals (2.92 spg) and minutes (36.2 mpg) over this stretch.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/12/03/november-rookies/index.html|title=Carter-Williams, McLemore named Kia NBA Rookies of Month|date=December 3, 2013|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=December 4, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131207010729/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/12/03/november-rookies/index.html|archive-date=December 7, 2013|url-status=dead}} He was again named Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month for games of January 2014. During January he led all rookies in scoring (16.5 ppg), and ranked second in rebounding (5.6 rpg), assists (5.6 apg) and minutes (33.3 mpg).{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/02/05/kia-rookies-of-month-january/index.html|title=Carter-Williams, Burke honored as January's top rookies|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=February 5, 2014|access-date=February 5, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140206174018/http://www.nba.com/2014/news/02/05/kia-rookies-of-month-january/index.html|archive-date=February 6, 2014|url-status=dead}} During the month of February, Carter-Williams participated in the [[BBVA Rising Stars Challenge]] and the [[Taco Bell Skills Challenge]].{{cite web|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/blogs/sports/sixers/Michael-Carter-Williams-enjoying-first-All-Star-weekend.html|title=Michael Carter-Williams enjoying first All-Star weekend|publisher=Philly.com|last=Cooney|first=Bob|date=February 14, 2014|access-date=August 9, 2014}} On March 10, 2014, Carter-Williams recorded his second career triple-double with 23 points, 10 assists, and 13 rebounds in a 123–110 loss to the New York Knicks.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140310/PHINYK/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Knicks 123, 76ers 110|last=Hamilton|first=Moke|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=March 10, 2014|access-date=August 11, 2014}} He became the first rookie in 76ers franchise history to record two triple doubles in a season. Carter-Williams was again named the Eastern Conference Rookie of the month for March 2014.{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2014084-michael-carter-williams-and-gorgui-dieng-named-rookies-of-the-month-for-march|title=Michael Carter-Williams and Gorgui Dieng Named Rookies of the Month for March|work=Bleacher Report|last=Babb|first=Stephen|date=April 1, 2014|access-date=August 9, 2014}} He is the first rookie in 76ers franchise history to be named conference rookie of the month three times. On April 14, 2014, Carter-Williams recorded 21 points and a career high 14 rebounds.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140414/BOSPHI/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Sixers 113, Celtics 108|last=Jones|first=Goldie|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=April 14, 2014|access-date=August 11, 2014}} The 14 rebounds were the most recorded by a point guard in the [[2013–14 NBA season]]. Carter-Williams finished his rookie season with averages of 16.7 ppg, 6.2 rpg, and 6.3 apg. At the time, he was one of only three players in NBA history to average 16 points, 6 rebounds and 6 assists in a rookie season, the other players being [[Oscar Robertson]] and [[Magic Johnson]],{{cite web|url=http://philly.barstoolsports.com/around-barstool/michael-carter-williams-becomes-only-third-rookie-besides-magic-johnson-oscar-robertson-to-average-1666/|title=Michael Carter-Williams Becomes Only Third Rookie Besides Magic Johnson & Oscar Robertson To Average 16/6/6|publisher=[[Barstool Sports]]|date=April 15, 2014|access-date=August 17, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140417054139/http://philly.barstoolsports.com/around-barstool/michael-carter-williams-becomes-only-third-rookie-besides-magic-johnson-oscar-robertson-to-average-1666/|archive-date=April 17, 2014}} though [[Luka Dončić]] later achieved it. On May 5, 2014, he was named the 2014 [[NBA Rookie of the Year]],{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/05/05/kia-rookie-of-the-year-official-release/|title=Philadelphia's Michael Carter-Williams named 2013–14 Kia NBA Rookie of the Year|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=May 5, 2014|access-date=August 8, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140505180315/http://www.nba.com/2014/news/05/05/kia-rookie-of-the-year-official-release/|archive-date=May 5, 2014|url-status=dead}} becoming the first rookie drafted 10th or later to win the award since [[Mark Jackson (basketball)|Mark Jackson]] in 1987. ====2014–15 season==== [[File:Michael Carter-Williams 2.jpg|thumb|Carter-Williams with the 76ers in 2014]] After undergoing shoulder surgery in May 2014,{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/10893171/michael-carter-williams-philadelphia-76ers-shoulder-surgery|title=Michael Carter-Williams has surgery|work=ESPN|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|agency=Associated Press|date=May 6, 2014|access-date=November 1, 2014}} Carter-Williams subsequently missed the [[2014 NBA Summer League]] and training camp, before later being ruled out for the start of the 2014–15 regular season as well.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/11749882/michael-carter-williams-philadelphia-76ers-eyes-nov-13-return|title=Carter-Williams eyes Nov. 13 return|last=Goodman|first=Jeff|work=ESPN|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=October 23, 2014|access-date=May 29, 2015}} Despite the injury, the 76ers exercised their third-year team option on Carter-Williams' rookie scale contract on October 31, extending the contract through the 2015–16 season.{{cite press release|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/141031-team-options|title=Sixers Exercise Team Options On Three Players|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=October 31, 2014|access-date=November 1, 2014}} Carter-Williams returned from injury on November 13 to make his season debut against the Dallas Mavericks. In 30 minutes off the bench, he recorded a team-high 19 points as well as 8 rebounds and 5 assists in a 123–70 loss.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141113/PHIDAL/gameinfo.html|title=Mavs get their biggest win ever, 123–70 over 76ers|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=November 13, 2014|access-date=November 14, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906114536/http://www.nba.com/games/20141113/PHIDAL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=September 6, 2015|url-status=dead}} On November 29, 2014, Carter-Williams recorded his third career triple-double with 18 points, 10 rebounds, and a career high 16 assists in a 110–103 loss to the Dallas Mavericks.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/141129-carter-williams-breakout|title=Carter-Williams Breaks Out With Triple-double; Grant Makes Debut|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|last=Ammon|first=Doug|date=November 29, 2014|access-date=November 29, 2014}} He went on to record his fourth career triple-double on December 13, 2014, with 16 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists in a 120–115 overtime loss to the Memphis Grizzles.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141213/MEMPHI/gameinfo.html|title=Conley's 36 lead Grizzlies past 76ers in overtime|last=Gelston|first=Dan|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=December 13, 2014|access-date=December 15, 2014}} On January 30, he recorded his fifth career triple-double with 17 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists in a 103–94 win over the Minnesota Timberwolves.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150130/MINPHI/gameinfo.html|title=Carter-Williams leads 76ers past Timberwolves 103–94|last=Bracy|first=Aaron|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=January 30, 2015|access-date=January 31, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170918024336/http://www.nba.com/games/20150130/MINPHI/gameinfo.html|archive-date=September 18, 2017|url-status=dead}} ===Milwaukee Bucks (2015–2016)=== On February 19, 2015, Carter-Williams was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in a three-team deal involving the [[Phoenix Suns]]. As part of the deal, Milwaukee also received [[Tyler Ennis (basketball)|Tyler Ennis]] and [[Miles Plumlee]] from Phoenix, while Phoenix received [[Brandon Knight (basketball)|Brandon Knight]] from Milwaukee, and Philadelphia received a future first-round pick from Phoenix via the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite press release|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-acquire-michael-carter-williams-tyler-ennis-and-miles-plumlee-three-team-trade|title=Bucks Acquire Michael Carter-Williams, Tyler Ennis and Miles Plumlee in Three-Team Trade|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=February 19, 2015|access-date=February 19, 2015}} On February 25, he made his debut for the Bucks, recording 7 points and 8 assists as a starter in a 104–88 win over his former team the Philadelphia 76ers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150225/PHIMIL/gameinfo.html|title=Carter-Williams impresses in debut, Bucks rout 76ers 104–88|last=Armas|first=Genaro C.|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=February 25, 2015|access-date=May 7, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150301123547/http://www.nba.com/games/20150225/PHIMIL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 1, 2015|url-status=dead}} On April 8, he scored a season-high 30 points in a loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150408/CLEMIL/gameinfo.html|title=Cavs clinch division, 2nd seed, 104–99 over Bucks|agency=Associated Press|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=April 8, 2015|access-date=May 7, 2015}} Five days later, he matched his season-high with 30 points in his first game back in Philadelphia since being traded to lead the Bucks to a 107–97 win over the 76ers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150413/MILPHI/gameinfo.html|title=Carter-Williams scores 30, Bucks beat 76ers 107–97|last=Bracy|first=Aaron|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=April 13, 2015|access-date=May 7, 2015}} Carter-Williams began the 2015–16 season strongly for the Bucks, averaging 12.8 points, 6.8 assists, 4.5 rebounds, 1.8 steals and 1.0 blocks over the first four games. He subsequently missed the next five games with an ankle injury, returning to action on November 14. He started in his first 11 games of the season before being moved to the bench on November 29 in favor of [[Jerryd Bayless]] after a string of poor performances – between November 14 and November 27, he averaged much lower numbers with 9.1 points, 3.7 assists, and 2.4 rebounds per game.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/cartemi01/gamelog/2016/ Michael Carter-Williams 2015–16 Game Log] On December 5, he had his best game since the season opener, recording 20 points, 5 assists and 3 rebounds off the bench in a 106–91 win over the New York Knicks.[http://www.nba.com/games/20151205/NYKMIL/gameinfo.html Carter-Williams leads Bucks to 106–91 win over Knicks] On January 8, he recorded 15 points and a season-high 12 rebounds in a 96–95 win over the Dallas Mavericks.[http://www.nba.com/games/20160108/DALMIL/gameinfo.html Middleton, Bucks beat Mavericks 96–95] On February 1, he recorded 18 points and a season-high 13 assists in a loss to the Sacramento Kings.[http://www.nba.com/games/20160201/MILSAC/gameinfo.html Gay scores 32 to lead Kings over Bucks, 111–104] On March 7, he was ruled out for the rest of the season with a torn labrum in his left hip.[http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/medical-update-michael-carter-williams MEDICAL UPDATE ON MICHAEL CARTER-WILLIAMS] ===Chicago Bulls (2016–2017)=== On October 17, 2016, Carter-Williams was traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in exchange for [[Tony Snell (basketball)|Tony Snell]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-acquire-michael-carter-williams-tony-snell|title=Bulls acquire Michael Carter-Williams for Tony Snell|work=NBA.com|date=October 17, 2016|access-date=October 17, 2016}} He made his debut for the Bulls in their season opener on October 27, 2016, recording five points, six rebounds and three assists off the bench in a 105–99 win over the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899422|title=Celtics vs. Bulls – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=October 27, 2016|access-date=November 1, 2016}} On November 1, 2016, he was ruled out for four to six weeks after he sustained a bone bruise with no ligament damage to his knee, as well as a left wrist sprain.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/michael-carter-williams-injury-update|title=Michael Carter-Williams injury update|work=NBA.com|date=November 1, 2016|access-date=November 1, 2016}} He returned to the Bulls lineup on December 26, 2016, and finished with one point (0-for-5 from the field) in 19 minutes against the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899907|title=Mirotic, Wade lead Bulls over Pacers 90–85 to snap skid at 3|work=ESPN.com|date=December 26, 2016|access-date=December 27, 2016}} On He appears on the [[ACC Network]] show ''Nothing But Net''.{{cite web |last1=Bradley |first1=Colin |title=Former Syracuse Star Michael Carter-Williams Joins ESPN as Men's College Basketball Analyst |url=https://espnpressroom.com/us/press-releases/2025/01/former-syracuse-star-michael-carter-williams-joins-espn-as-mens-college-basketball-analyst/ |website=ESPN Press Room U.S. |access-date=7 January 2025 |date=7 January 2025}} In May 2025, Carter-Williams fought in a charity [[boxing]] event and won by decision. He has stated plans to continue fighting and potentially pursue a career in the sport. ==Personal life== Carter-Williams is the son of Earl Williams and Mandy Zegarowski (née Carter) and step-son of Zach Zegarowski and Rosa Williams.
